title: Grateful Dead Live at Youth Opportunities Center on 1966-02-12

ai_review.summary: Rough early‑1966 soundboard capture of an Acid Test jam with Pigpen’s raw vocal fire; historically fascinating but audio is noisy and Jerry is absent.
ai_review.review: The recording offers a gritty glimpse into the 1966 Acid Tests, spotlighting Pigpen’s passionate vocals and a historic “Foolish > Walkin’ Blues > Day Job” finale. While many listeners love the raw energy and historical value, the soundboard tape is low‑fidelity and some find it more noise than music, especially noting Jerry Garcia’s absence.

ai_rating.rationale: Average of ten reviews (≈3.8) with strong praise for Pigpen and historic moments but consistent complaints about audio quality and missing guitar, yielding a solid‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Low‑fidelity tape that sounds like an outdoor/venue recording; muffled in places, occasional intrusive drum kick, overall noisy but captures the ambience of the Acid Test.

standout_songs: Pigpen rap segment (early Acid Test jam)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A chaotic, spoken‑word heavy set typical of early Acid Tests; little structured song work, more experimental vocal jams and spontaneous moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Not present on this recording; reviewers explicitly note his absence.
band_member_comments.Bob: His vocals are praised for raw passion; one reviewer wishes he’d stay quiet during Pigpen’s rap, another enjoys the Bobby‑Pigpen interaction.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboard contributions are mentioned positively, especially in hopes of hearing him sing with Pigpen.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum kick is called out as intrusive in at least one review.
